lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon la concentración:
"

With a fixed enzyme concentration, the rate rises with [S] and saturates when all enzymes are occupied (Vmax = kcat·[E]ₜ). Km is the [S] at which v = Vmax/2. Here each enzyme binds, converts and releases substrates at random; the actual rate is measured.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa actividad depende:
"

Activity depends on the pH (ionization state of the residues) and on the temperature (it increases ≈ ×2 for every 10 °C until the protein denatures). On unfolding the active site is lost: the loss is largely irreversible.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa catálisis \u003cb\:
"

Catalysis lowers the activation energy (from ≈ 75 to ≈ 45 kJ/mol) by stabilizing the transition state; the rate increases ≈ 10⁵-fold (e^{ΔΔG‡/RT}). The enzyme does not change the ΔG of the reaction or the equilibrium.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eSe forma el \u003cb\u:
"

The enzyme–substrate complex (ES) forms; the catalytic residues strain the bond up to the transition state ES‡; the bond breaks and the products leave. The enzyme remains intact and ready for another cycle.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn inhibidor \u003cb\:
"

A competitive inhibitor occupies the active site (apparent Km ↑, Vmax unchanged; overcome with more substrate). A noncompetitive inhibitor binds to another site (allosteric) and deforms the enzyme (Vmax ↓, Km unchanged). In Lineweaver–Burk: the lines intersect on the y axis (competitive) or on the x axis (noncompetitive).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUna enzima une al \u0:
"

An enzyme binds the substrate at its active site. Lock-and-key model: the active site is already complementary; induced fit model: the enzyme reshapes itself on binding the substrate. A wrongly shaped substrate does not fit: that is enzyme specificity.

"
lit.\u0027a un sitio distinto del activo\u00: "to a site other than the active one"
lit.\u0027Agrega un inhibidor competitivo y: 'Add a competitive inhibitor and then a non-competitive one: compare Km and Vmax on Lineweaver–Burk.'

lit.\u0027Cada enzima tiene un óptimo; fuera: "Each enzyme has an optimum; outside it, it denatures"
